rows.text: - **Why $h$ and not just some Riemannian metric.** The particular combination $g+2n^\flat\otimes n^\flat$ has the additional property, recorded in [[lem-gr-causal-curve-conventions]] and used in the limit-curve arguments, that $h(X,X)\ge1$ for every $g$-unit future timelike $X$; this is what makes the arclength depth of prepended geodesics controlled without completeness assumptions on $g$.

rows.text: Clause (a) is the statement that the $h$-speed of an affine velocity changes at most exponentially in $h$-arclength on compact regions; clause (b) is the affine continuation used in [[lem-gr-boundary-null-geodesic-segment]] to rule out an implicit affine-completeness assumption for boundary geodesics. The hypothesis of clause (b) is met in applications for the auxiliary metric of [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]], and the finite-length hypothesis is automatic when the tail is confined to a compact set of a strongly causal spacetime, by [[lem-gr-strong-causality-compact-length-bound]]; that composition is used in [[lem-gr-boundary-null-geodesic-segment]].
